title: Average asking rent down 2.9% in B.C. in September, marking 2 years of decreases: report
description: A monthly report from Rentals.ca and Urbanation said the figures mark two full years of annual declines, the longest downturn the Canadian rental market has experienced in recent history.

title: Asking rents drop again, but B.C. remains among Canada's most expensive markets
description: Asking rents in British Columbia continue to fall, sliding by 4.5 per cent year over year in July, according to a new report.

title: Vancouver Giants to move to Surrey as city announces 10,000-seat arena
description: A new 10,000-seat arena is being built in Surrey, B.C., and the city has secured the Vancouver Giants as the anchor tenant.

title: Carney defends $1.45B plan to convert unbought B.C. condos to affordable rent-to-own
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney says the provincial and federal governments have done a poor job of explaining their plan to buy unsold, vacant condos in B.C. and turn them into affordable housing. He shared new details on the plan Thursday.

title: Vancouver renters fear eviction amid proposed hotel in Mount Pleasant
description: Residents in a Mount Pleasant rental building are sounding the alarm over a proposed hotel that they say would displace them. The project is being proposed under the city's Broadway Plan, which was designed with tenant protections in mind. But renters say there's minimal protections when housing is replaced by hotels.

title: B.C. supportive housing bill aims to increase safety. Critics fear it will push problems onto streets
description: Those opposed to Bill 11 fear it will drive up evictions, increase homelessness and push problems onto the streets. But proponents say it will make supportive housing buildings safer for tenants and staff.

title: Vancouver School Board loses appeal over developer's lowered rent for Kingsgate Mall
description: The Vancouver School Board (VSB) has failed in its bid to have the B.C. Court of Appeal overturn lowered rent for the Kingsgate Mall site. A lower court had ruled that Beedie Developments should pay VSB $1.65 million per year for the East Vancouver site, and not the $9.6 million per year that an arbitration panel had suggested.

title: B.C. legislation aims to crack down on weapons, violence in supportive housing
description: Groups like the B.C. Coalition of Safe and Supportive Housing have long raised concerns about weapons and violence from tenants, and Housing Minister Christine Boyle says the legislation responds to those concerns.

title: This Nanaimo senior challenged years of rent increases, and won
description: Shane Conn challenged two years of rent increases at a Nanaimo independent living facility at the Residential Tenancy Board. He won and received almost $9,500 in rent deductions and a limit on future increases. But the benefits apply only to him. They don’t apply to any of his neighbours unless they go through the same months-long administrative process Conn did.

title: ‘Knowing your rights’: Prince George, B.C., renters forming tenants union
description: Renters in Prince George, B.C., are coming together to form a tenants union to advocate for renters rights, as the cost of housing in the city rises.

title: Data shows improved affordability, safety metrics in Vancouver — leading to political credit and caution
description: Just as the provincial government has sent out multiple releases crediting their policies for the decrease in rent, ABC Vancouver is happy to take credit for other metrics changing.

title: Metro Vancouver mayors urge B.C. to roll back housing density laws, but province ‘not going backwards’
description: A coalition of Metro Vancouver mayors is calling on the B.C. government to repeal housing legislation designed to increase supply through higher density, but the housing minister says there's no going "backward."

title: Surrey, B.C., family fears for safety after extortion task force raids home
description: Sameer Arora says a 25-person extortion task force squad raided his family’s home last month while carrying out a search warrant related to their basement suite tenant. Now, the family worries they've inadvertently been put at risk.

title: After controversial land deal, Vancouver school's basketball courts are set to become rental housing
description: Parents are frustrated with a recent Vancouver city council decision to rezone a portion of land owned by the school board to allow a six-storey rental building.

title: B.C. Greens want to tie rent increases to units, not tenants – but face uphill battle
description: A B.C. Green MLA bill this week aims to create vacancy control – a policy that would limit rent increases by tying them to a unit, not an individual tenancy. It's generated support from poverty reduction and tenants’ rights groups – however, one economist warns it could spark unintended consequences for the housing market.

title: Landlord threatened to evict Vancouver tenants over posts in private Facebook group
description: Residents of The Yarrow in East Vancouver say their landlord, Realstar Group, made false accusations when it sent them letters threatening to evict them for discussing issues in a tenants' Facebook group. The company has since apologized.

title: Feds lend developer $763M to build almost 1,300 rentals in Burnaby, B.C.
description: Development company Grosvenor said the loan, provided through the Apartment Construction Loan Program (ACLP), will finance the construction of 1,279 rental homes at the Brentwood Block development on Lougheed Highway in Burnaby, B.C.

title: B.C. judge overturns eviction of 73-year-old renter, citing landlord's 'questionable' practices
description: A vulnerable tenant won a B.C. Supreme Court challenge to overturn an eviction, as the judge said the Residential Tenancy Branch arbitrator did not adequately assess if the landlord’s eviction notice was done in good faith.

title: UBC to build replacement low-income rental building after alleged construction damage evicted tenants
description: The University of British Columbia will build a replacement subsidized apartment building for a Kelowna, B.C., non-profit, after the old building was allegedly damaged by construction last year. But one tenant is concerned former renters won't be included in the new building.

title: B.C. sets rent increase cap at 2.3% in 2026, down from this year's 3%
description: Next year's maximum allowable rent increase is tied to the Consumer Price Index, the province says.

title: Landlords say Ruby Liu's plan for Bay properties 'defies commercial common sense'
description: In filings made with the Ontario Superior Court on Saturday, Cadillac Fairview says it is “resolutely opposed” to Liu becoming a tenant at some of its malls because she has no detailed or credible business plan.

title: Volleyball and velodrome groups face uncertain future in Burnaby, B.C.
description: Burnaby, B.C., councillors voted to open a call for a lease on the Harry Jerome Sports Centre, but the decision has caused anxiety for long-time tenants Volleyball B.C. and the Burnaby Velodrome Club.

title: Metro Vancouver's condo market is slumping. Here are 4 key factors behind the slowdown
description: After years of soaring prices, Metro Vancouver's condo market is showing signs of strain, with projects stalling and sales declining. Industry experts say it’s the result of four major forces converging: high interest rates and softening rental income, reduced foreign capital and lower immigration.

title: Bullet holes and police raids: Former real estate agent investigated for allegedly subletting to criminals
description: A former Lower Mainland real estate agent is under investigation by the industry's regulator after his name emerged as the tenant on multiple suites raided last year during a Vancouver police investigation into a major drug trafficking gang.

title: B.C.'s Official Opposition calls for changes to supportive housing following CBC investigation into death
description: British Columbia's Official Opposition is calling for widespread changes to supportive housing in the province following a CBC News investigation that revealed an 11-day delay in finding the body of a tenant.

title: Non-profit thrift stores in Metro Vancouver struggle as rents soar
description: The operators of non-profit thrift stores in Metro Vancouver say the region's expensive real estate market is making it difficult for them to make money, and that's keeping them from being able to help their communities.

title: This Vancouver housing co-op is facing a $1M tax if it wants to renew its lease for more than 30 years
description: Right now, rent at the co-op goes up about three per cent annually to build up reserves for maintenance. To accommodate the property transfer tax, it would have to go up at least seven per cent for several years.

title: Metro Vancouver housing prices may lower amid economic uncertainty, experts say
description: Greater Vancouver real estate experts say the economic uncertainty caused by Canada's recent election and its ongoing trade war with the U.S. mean sellers may have to lower prices to convince buyers that now is a good time to spend.

title: Oak Bay tenant calls for provincial, municipal tenant support following 'renoviction'
description: A two-year tenancy branch battle ended in eviction for a group of Oak Bay renters last month, after their landlord successfully argued he needed the building emptied to perform renovations. Now, one of those tenants is speaking up and calling for better tenant supports.

title: Pace of rent increases slows, but housing costs still rising in Metro Vancouver
description: The pace of rent increases in Metro Vancouver slowed last year compared with 2023, and the rental stock is growing, but there's a shortage of units for families, and the wait-list for social housing is getting longer, a new report has found.

title: Ontario home destroyed in 'suspicious' fire hours before tenant vacate order took effect
description: A B.C. resident who's the executor in charge of an Ontario farmhouse co-owned by her father is frustrated it took months to get a legal order to get a person she describes as a squatter off the property north of Goderich. Hours before the order came into effect, the house was destroyed in a suspicious fire.

title: UBC denies its downtown Kelowna campus construction caused full extent of damage to surrounding buildings
description: The University of British Columbia has denied causing the full extent of the damage to buildings surrounding its Kelowna, B.C., downtown campus construction site in response to a lawsuit filed against the university and other parties by tenants forced to evacuate their homes last year.

title: Province trying to seize property used to build drug superlab in rural B.C.
description: B.C. Civil Forfeiture Office is alleging that a rural property owner should have known about the drug activity happening on his land. But the owner is denying any wrongdoing and blaming his tenants.

title: More vacancies but higher average rent prices forecast for Metro Vancouver: CMHC
description: The Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation says new pricier rental units entering the market over the next couple of years will drive up the average cost of rent, but that a decrease in overall demand will help affordability.

title: B.C. construction industry warns of increased costs as Trump talks tariffs against lumber
description: The looming trade war has sparked uncertainty in B.C.'s housing market, with developers worried that the already sky-high cost of new construction is about to be driven up even further.

title: Could Montreal rents reach Toronto and Vancouver levels of unaffordability?
description: Tenants's rights groups are calling for a rent hike freeze until measures such as a mandatory rental registry and a ceiling on rent hikes are implemented.

title: B.C. housing minister says Vancouver's plan for Downtown Eastside could increase crime
description: B.C. Housing Minister Ravi Kahlon says Vancouver Mayor Ken Sim's new plan for the Downtown Eastside will make the community less safe and lead to more homelessness.

title: Developer wins multimillion-dollar rent dispute with Vancouver School Board
description: A Vancouver developer will pay almost $8 million less in rent to the city's school board, after the B.C. Supreme Court issued a ruling on the school-owned Kingsgate Mall property.

title: Months after displacement, Kelowna tenants feel forgotten as UBC construction continues
description: Tenants of a Kelowna, B.C., subsidized housing building say they feel scattered and forgotten after being displaced earlier this spring due to unsafe conditions in the building from ground settling linked to a UBC Okanagan construction site next door.

title: B.C. tenant faces legal and financial hurdles to reclaim rental suite after landlord locked her out
description: A B.C. woman is fighting to reclaim her rental suite at a Lumby, B.C., motel after being locked out by her landlord in August, despite a court order and a ruling from the Residential Tenancy Branch in her favour.

title: Remaining CRAB Park residents ordered out as Vancouver enforces eviction
description: The seven remaining residents of Vancouver's CRAB Park encampment began moving out on Thursday after more than three years of living there.

title: Vancouver Park Board to close homeless encampment at CRAB Park
description: The CRAB Park encampment began in 2021, remaining in place in 2022 when a B.C. Supreme Court judge set aside eviction notices partially because the city didn't have enough indoor shelter spaces to accommodate those living at the camp.

title: 40-year-old B.C. brewery closing facility after 35% rent hike
description: One of the oldest craft breweries in British Columbia is shutting down its main facility and outsourcing production and packaging duties to a nearby brewery, citing a large hike in rent at its Victoria location.

title: B.C. sets rent increase cap at 3% for 2025
description: The B.C. government says landlords will not be able to increase rents by more than three per cent in 2025.

title: Lobby group pushes B.C. party leaders to repeal rent restrictions
description: Sparked by frustrations over new short-term rental restrictions, a lobby group of short-term rental owners is attempting to influence B.C. Conservative and B.C. United party leaders' housing policies.

title: Tenant advocate decries RTB's 27% rent increase decision
description: A lawyer and renters' advocate says investors shouldn't be insulated from losses by provincial regulations when they make risky bets on the housing market.

title: B.C. tenancy branch allows 2 landlords to hike rent by 23.5%
description: In a recent decision, the Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB) allowed a pair of B.C. landlords to raise rent by 23.5 per cent over two years — on top of the province's annual allowable rent increase of 3.5 per cent.

title: B.C. court overturns RTB decision evicting man on disability
description: The B.C. Supreme Court has overturned a Residential Tenancy Branch (RTB) decision that permitted the eviction of a Vancouver man on disability who spent months dealing with the fallout from the ministry's $45 underpayment of his rent last year.

title: 21 tenants to be evicted from transitional housing in Vancouver
description: A Coast Mental Health project that provides people with temporary transitional housing and access to supportive care for a range of mental and physical disabilities will end July 31.

title: Calls increase for heat limits in B.C. rental housing
description: Ecotrust Canada is asking B.C. municipalities to adopt bylaws requiring rental units to maintain livable temperature ranges during periods of extreme heat.

title: B.C. seniors vulnerable to illegal rent increases: advocate
description: The B.C. seniors advocate said that an investigation by his team found some landlords are routinely failing to comply with basic B.C. rental rules.

title: B.C. government to launch website to combat 'bad faith' evictions
description: The Ministry of Housing says the Landlord Use Web Portal will go live on July 18 and will require landlords to generate eviction notices under the Residential Tenancy Act's provision allowing tenants to be evicted from a unit if a family member or caretaker intends to move in.

title: New Westminster, B.C., council votes to boost renters' protection
description: Council in New Westminster, B.C., has passed a motion to beef up renters' protections after new provincial legislation on housing density raised fears that tenants in affordable homes could be forced out by redevelopment.

title: Metro Vancouver tree canopy in decline amid push for new housing
description: A report presented to Metro Vancouver's regional government on Friday says leafy, tree-lined neighbourhoods are under threat from increased growth and densification as cities face pressure, including requirements from the provincial government, to build vast amounts of new housing.

title: Disabled people overrepresented in study of evicted tenants
description: A recently-released Statistics Canada study of evicted tenants found that disabled people are overrepresented among recent evictees, and no-fault evictions are the most common reason for a tenancy to be terminated.

title: Evacuation of Kelowna, B.C., apartment near construction site extended for 2 weeks
description: Hadgraft Wilson Place, which serves low-income tenants, was evacuated Tuesday because of concerns over construction activity at nearby University of British Columbia-Okanagan.

title: Low-income tenants told to leave over UBC construction site risk
description: More than 80 residents of a low-income apartment building in Kelowna, B.C., have been told they need to leave because a nearby construction site has caused a "significant" risk to life and safety.

title: Renting? You probably report lower quality of life than homeowners
description: Statistics Canada says survey results over the last few years show renters are more prone to reporting a lower quality of life than homeowners, especially in Vancouver and Toronto.

title: B.C. family facing eviction says tenancy laws need to change
description: A family in Maple Ridge, B.C. who challenged their eviction and lost say they are at risk of homelessness after being ordered to move within eight days. — a situation one tenant advocate says is far too common under B.C.’s eviction rules.

title: B.C. continues to lead the country in high rental prices and low vacancies, CMHC data shows
description: When it comes to the rental market, Metro Vancouver continues to be at the top — or depending on how you look at the numbers, the bottom.

title: Cost of Metro Vancouver rental housing projects nearly doubles before construction begins
description: Among the reasons cited by Metro Vancouver for the increased budget were higher construction costs, an increase in parking area and bike storage lockers, and an increase to the size of a child care facility.

title: B.C. couple evict black bear after it attempts to den under their home
description: A couple on Vancouver Island were shocked to learn that a black bear had set up a den underneath their home.

title: Vancouver landlord acted in bad faith in attempted eviction for caretaker use, arbitrator finds
description: Vancouver property management company Plan A Real Estate Services acted in bad faith when it tried to evict a tenant to make space for a live-in building caretaker, B.C.’s Residential Tenancy Branch has found.

title: Full-time residents of North Vancouver marina learn they won't be evicted after all
description: Just days after being told they needed to vacate their homes within the next six months, about 200 full-time residents of a North Vancouver marina have been told they’ll be allowed to stay.

title: As B.C. moves towards encampment injunction change, homeless people call for moratorium on winter evictions
description: Homeless and formerly unhoused residents of Vancouver's Downtown Eastside raised alarms on Wednesday about what they said is ongoing displacement from public spaces.

title: Vancouver leads the way as Canadian rent prices hit new high for 6th month in a row: report
description: The average asking price for a rental unit in Canada reached $2,178 last month, a 9.9 per cent year-over-year increase and continuing a trend that has seen asking rents hit new highs for six months in a row.

title: Residents and advocates rally, pack court for Vancouver's appeal of struck-down SRO housing rules
description: The City of Vancouver is appealing an August 2022 ruling that struck down its bylaw limiting how much property owners could increase the rents of single-room occupancy (SRO) housing between tenancies.

title: B.C. food banks struggle to keep up as demand across Canada soars
description: The Greater Vancouver Food Bank says more and more people are accessing its services each year, and with greater frequency than in the past as low wages and high rents squeeze people between inflation and other rising costs.

title: Changes to caretaker provision in B.C. eviction laws needed, tenants' rights lawyer says
description: A tenants rights lawyer is asking the B.C. government to strengthen eviction laws to address what he calls an emerging trend of "shotgun evictions," where multiple tenants in a building are told they face possible eviction so a caretaker can move in.

title: Key New Brunswick tenant protection policy dealt a setback in court decision
description: A pair of investors from Coquitlam, B.C., who bought a Saint John apartment building in 2022 and financed the purchase with a large variable-rate mortgage, are having some success challenging a provincial government rent control policy.

title: Unhoused seniors say search for affordable housing in Metro Vancouver turns up 'nothing, nothing, nothing'
description: According to the Homelessness Services Association of B.C., 22 per cent of people who reported being homeless were age 55 or older, compared to about 10 per cent of those counted in 2005.

title: Vancouver staff recommend raising the rents in affordable housing pilot program
description: The City of Vancouver wants to increase the rates for moderate income rental housing as part of a strategy to build more affordable homes, but a former city councillor says the initiative is just a way for developers to make more money.

title: This B.C. landlord was shocked to find his rental suite listed on Airbnb. Now, he wants stricter regulations
description: A landlord in Vancouver is calling on the provincial government to tighten regulations for short-term rentals after he was surprised to find out his tenant was illegally listing his suite on Airbnb.

title: Feds' GST plan makes building B.C. rentals more 'palatable' but renter relief still a long way off: experts
description: B.C. developers are positioned to save millions of dollars building new rental units under Ottawa's latest measure to incentivize housing construction, but experts say it's unlikely renters will soon see much relief in markets like Metro Vancouver.

title: Both tenants and landlords express dismay at rent increase rate for 2024
description: In a market where rents continue to rise and many landlords rely on rental income to help cover their mortgages, both owners and tenants have expressed dismay over the announcement.

title: B.C. raises allowable rent increase to 3.5% for 2024
description: Landlords in B.C. will be allowed to raise rents up to 3.5 per cent in 2024, which the province says balances affordability for tenants and the ability for landlords to continue to maintain rental units.

title: Family evicted from townhouse awarded $27.7K to be paid by the buyer after sale falls through
description: The would-be purchaser was ordered to pay compensation of 12 months' rent even though they weren’t able to complete the subject-free sale because their financing didn’t come through. They also lost a $30,000 deposit.

title: Video promoting $2,000 rent for 200-square-foot Vancouver apartment widely criticized
description: The rents for newly renovated studio units at the Lotus Hotel had been publicly listed for $1,995 a month for some time, but it took a viral TikTok video to spark a larger conversation about the property — and the state of renting in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside.

title: With temperatures set to hit high 30s in B.C., housing advocates call for heat limits in rental homes
description: Advocates for renters in B.C. say it's time to consider setting a maximum temperature for rental housing to protect vulnerable tenants from dangerous heat. The call comes as a heat wave blankets much of the province, raising memories of the deadly 2021 heat dome.

title: Candles sparked Mount Pleasant blaze that evicted dozens, fire department says
description: Vancouver Fire Rescue Services says the fire at 414 East 10th Ave has been deemed accidental — although the department has submitted fire bylaw offences for prosecution against the building owners.

title: Landlords in B.C. warning renters against installing AC units despite rising heat
description: CBC has verified that notices have been issued to tenants in multiple buildings under at least two different management companies, just weeks after the province of B.C. announced a program to provide air conditioners to eligible British Columbians.

title: As housing costs soar, some financial analysts advise to scrap the 30% rule
description: Thirty per cent is the often-touted maximum percentage of your income that you should spend on a home. But in an age where the average one-bedroom apartment in Vancouver rents for $2,787 a month, is that number still realistic?

title: Metro Vancouver renters could take the hit as condo investments become less viable
description: According to data from the Canadian Mortgage and Housing Corporation, condos owned and rented out by private investors make up about 40 per cent of all market-rate apartments in Metro Vancouver.

title: Would you pay $800 a month to live in a closet? In Vancouver, that may be all you can afford
description: Exorbitant rents in Metro Vancouver are nothing new, but renters in the region say the listings they’re coming across have reached a whole new level of absurdity.

title: B.C. has highest no-fault eviction rate in Canada, but landlords say rules make valid evictions too difficult
description: British Columbia has the highest rate of no-fault evictions in Canada, but some landlords say the province's tenancy rules make it too hard for landlords to raise rent and evict tenants for valid reasons.

title: More B.C. tenants are evicted through no fault of their own than anywhere else in Canada, report says
description: Renters in British Columbia face the highest eviction rates in Canada by far, but it’s through no fault of their own, according to a new report from researchers at the University of British Columbia.

title: Agree to 40% rent hike or we may sell your homes, landlord tells Surrey, B.C., renters
description: Tenants in Surrey are devastated after their landlord made the steep demand. A tenants’ rights advocate says while the situation has some unusual aspects, landlords are free to seek agreements for higher rent — and many do.

title: Many supportive housing tenants in B.C.'s Central Okanagan aren't getting the care they need: study
description: According to the study, published in the May 2023 issue of B.C. Medical Journal, 72 per cent of supportive housing tenants reported feeling their health needs had gone unmet.

title: Vancouver risks becoming a 'city without art' as studio spaces become harder to find, artists say
description: Artists in Vancouver say they are struggling to find permanent spaces to create their art amid rising rents and increasing development.

title: Province announces 'historic' agreement with Metro Vancouver, B.C. Housing to build 2,000 affordable homes
description: The province, B.C. Housing and the Metro Vancouver Regional District announced Wednesday that they have signed a memorandum of understanding agreeing to construct 2,000 affordable homes over the next 10 years.

title: Unaffordable affordable homes: Rent at some single room occupancy units more than $1,000
description: Across downtown Vancouver, there are more than 160 single-room occupancy [SRO] buildings that contain small single rooms, usually with a shared kitchen and bathroom facilities.

title: Soaring rents in Toronto, Vancouver force residents on modest incomes into 'deplorable' conditions
description: With Vancouver and Toronto vacancy rates at less than two per cent and rental prices surging, residents on modest or fixed incomes are being priced out of their communities and forced into what one expert calls 'deplorable' conditions.

title: Why rent is so expensive in 3 Canadian cities (that aren't Toronto or Vancouver)
description: Across the country, it's getting harder and more expensive to find a place to rent — and not just in Toronto and Vancouver.

title: Rents in B.C. continue to be highest in the country, says yearly federal report
description: Overall, the average price of a two-bedroom apartment across all B.C. communities with at least 10,000 people was $1,721, up 11 per cent from 2021 and the highest figure for any province in Canada.
